basis: 2tor, Inc. is the earlier name of 2U, which the firm lists (partnered 2011, Rob Stavis; the archived 2012 list carries it as '2tor'); Rob Stavis is the director on the 2011 and 2012 filings. The same company as base row 2u, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row 2u (2tor renamed 2U in 2012). Bessemer led the $32.5M round of March 2011 (Form D 2011 Q1, Rob Stavis joins the board; the firm's own invest date is 2011-03-04), the company's fourth priced round after three in 2009 and 2010, so Growth; model, the round's press page was not retrieved. Headquarters moved from Lanham, Maryland to Arlington, Virginia. Graduation not applicable.

basis: Adaptive Planning, Inc. is the earlier name of Adaptive Insights, which the firm lists (partnered 2013, Bob Goodman and Byron Deeter; the archived 2013 list carries it as 'Adaptive Planning, Inc.'), and the company's S-1 names Bessemer Venture Partners VIII as a holder. The same company as base row adaptive-insights, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row adaptive-insights. Acq. by Workday, 2018. Bessemer entered in the $45M round of May 2013 (Form D 2013 Q2; the S-1 has Byron Deeter on the board since May 2013), a late round of a company founded in 2003 with a $22M round the year before, so Growth; model, the round's own name was not found (the S-1 lists only the 2015 Series G).

basis: Hyper Labs, Inc. is the legal name of Hyperscience (New York; the filings carry its $60M, $80M and $100M rounds of 2020 to 2022 with Elliott Robinson as director), which the firm lists (partnered 2020, Elliott Robinson). The same company as base row hyperscience, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row hyperscience. The firm's own post: Bessemer leads the $60M Series C (June 2020), and its list dates the partnership to 2020, so the entry is the Series C, Growth; this disputes the Form D band, which read a 2018 filing with no Bessemer person on it. No valuation was disclosed at the $100M Series E of December 2021 (FinSMEs, read 2026-10-01), so the row stays below $1B.

basis: Justin.tv, Inc. is the corporate entity of Twitch: the firm's own memo says 'we would be investing in the Justin.tv corporate entity which includes both Twitch.tv and Justin.tv', and the firm lists Twitch (partnered 2012). The same company as base row twitch, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row twitch. Acq. by Amazon, 2014 (about $970M). The firm's own investment memo of July 2012 is headed 'Twitch Series B' and recommends $13M at $53M pre-money, so the entry is the Series B, Growth, against the Form D band's Series A; the firm's own invest date is 2012-09-11.

basis: Dolores Labs, Inc. is the legal name of CrowdFlower (later Figure Eight), which the firm lists from 2010 with an investment date of 2009-12-08, the first-sale date on this Form D; James Cham, then a Bessemer vice president, is the director. The same company as base row crowdflower, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row crowdflower. Acq. by Appen, 2019, as Figure Eight (Finovate, 2019-04-18, names Bessemer among its investors). The $5.1M round of December 2009 on the Form D was CrowdFlower's Series A, from Trinity Ventures and Bessemer, after a 2009 seed; model, the announcement page was not retrieved, so this disputes the band's Seed at medium confidence.

basis: PinPT, Inc. is the legal name of Pinpoint (Jeff Haynie's engineering-analytics company), which the firm listed in 2019 to 2022 and whose $13.5M Series A the firm's own post says it led; Ethan Kurzweil is the director on the 2018 filing. The same company as base row pinpoint, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row pinpoint. The firm dropped Pinpoint from its list after 2022 and its chief executive Jeff Haynie joined Shopmonkey as chief technology officer in June 2022 (GlobeNewswire), which says nothing of a sale or a shutdown; no later trace found (Google News, 2026-10-01), so the status reads unknown.

basis: Shop My Shelf, Inc. is the legal name of ShopMy, which the firm lists (partnered 2025, Jeremy Levine) and whose $77.5M Series B the firm's own post says it led; Jeremy Levine is the director on the 2025 filing. The same company as base row shopmy, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row shopmy. ShopMy raised $70M at a $1.5B valuation on 2025-10-22 (the company's release), the mark the Bain Capital Ventures book also carries. The Form D address is a founder's (Holden, Massachusetts); the company is in New York.

basis: Tinz Optics, Inc. is the legal name of Light, the multi-lens camera company, which the firm listed from 2014 with an investment date of 2014-05-09; Bob Goodman is the director on the 2014 filing of its $9M round. The same company as base row light, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row light. John Deere bought Light's patents and intellectual property and hired its team in May 2022 (Precision Farming Dealer), a sale of the business's core, so acquired (acq. by Deere, 2022), as the GV book reads it.

basis: Recover Together, Inc. is the legal name of Groups (Groups Recover Together), which the firm lists (partnered 2017, Steve Kraus); Steve Kraus is the director on the 2017 and 2021 filings. The same company as base row groups, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row groups. The firm's own post says 'We led the Series A of ... Groups', and its list dates the investment to 2017-04-11, so the entry is the Series A, against the Form D band's Seed (a $1.2M filing of June 2017). Headquarters Burlington, Massachusetts (the 2021 filings).

basis: K2 Global Consulting is the earlier name of K2 Intelligence, now K2 Integrity, which the firm lists (partnered 2010, Rob Stavis; the archived 2012 list carries it as 'K2 Global Consulting'); Eric Arnold, then on the firm's team, is the director on the 2010 filings. The same company as base rows k2-intelligence and k2-integrity, a duplicate group.

note: Same company as base rows k2-intelligence and k2-integrity (renamed K2 Integrity in November 2020). An investigations and risk-advisory firm, outside the focus taxonomy. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

basis: ReputationDefender is the earlier name of Reputation.com, now Reputation, which the firm lists (partnered 2009, David Cowan; the archived 2010 list carries it as 'ReputationDefender'); David Cowan is the director on the 2010 filing. The same company as base row reputation, a duplicate pair.

note: Same company as base row reputation. The firm's own invest date is 2009-04-17, the $5.4M round on the company's 2009 Form D; the company, founded in 2006, had already raised two venture rounds (2007 and 2008), so the entry is a third round, Growth; model, no page naming the 2009 round was retrieved. The consumer business was sold in 2018 and the enterprise company continues as Reputation, now in San Ramon, California.
